session_covered: US and European sessions of Wednesday 21 October
intro: Covers the US and European sessions of Wednesday 21 October. Delayed from the usual early send because the US session had not closed at 06:30; S&P 500 sector percentages are not available and several figures are reconciled (see footnotes).
footnotes: US 10-year: AP reported 5.12% (earlier snapshot), FNArena and Yahoo 5.15%, Trading Economics 5.13%; 5.15% used. Brent: AP reported a US$108.82 settlement; FNArena and Trading Economics show 109.63 later, used here. Gold is spot; December futures were about US$4,150-4,160. AUD/USD is a single-source CFD price (Trading Economics); iron ore is single-source (FNArena).

setup.summary: SPI 200 futures were around 8,848 (Dec contract 8,844), marginally lower, down roughly 0.01-0.21% (midpoint about -0.1%); three sources agree on a flat-to-slightly-lower direction despite Wall Street's gains. Applied to the prior ASX 200 close of 8,831.30 (+14.40 pts, +0.16% on Wednesday), that implies an open about 10 points (0.1%) lower, around 8,822 (range roughly 8,813-8,830).

local_events: AGMs for BHP, Brambles, IAG, Aurizon, ASX Ltd, APA Group, Cleanaway and others
Quarterly updates from Fortescue, Santos, Mirvac and Karoon
what_moved: Tech led Wall Street higher. SpaceX rose 7.8% after a stronger-than-expected profit and Nvidia gained 2.5%, the biggest single contributor to the S&P 500's rise, which left the index about 0.8% below its record. Netflix (-5.3%) and AT&T (-6.4%) fell on soft outlooks. The Treasury 10-year yield held near 5.12-5.15% and Brent stayed in the US$108-111 range amid the Iran conflict. S&P 500 sector percentages are not available.

news.headline: SpaceX profit lifts tech.
news.summary: SpaceX jumped 7.8% on a stronger summer profit, and Musk said it had taken a step to consider a possible merger with Tesla (+3.4%).

news.headline: Outlooks hit Netflix and AT&T.
news.summary: Both fell despite stronger profits, on forecasts below analyst expectations.

news.headline: Treasury yields steady near 5.1%.
news.summary: Markets price about 85% odds the Fed holds at its 27-28 October meeting and about 75% odds of a 25 bp hike in December.

news.headline: Oil stays elevated on Middle East risk.
news.summary: Brent has swung between US$97 and US$112 through October on the Iran war; reported strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi energy facilities supported prices.

news.headline: RBA hike bets build.
news.summary: The Australian dollar rose to about US$0.7026; markets price roughly 44% odds of an RBA hike on 3 November and 64% by December.

news.headline: ASX tech sell-off.
news.summary: The ASX 200 rose 0.16% on Wednesday, but the IT sector fell 3.32% as NextDC dropped over 40% on an earnings downgrade tied to data-centre power delays.

news.headline: UK inflation 3.5%.
news.summary: UK September CPI was 3.5% y/y and ANZ expects the Bank of England to raise rates to 4.0% next month.

coming_up: Australian September CPI on Wednesday 28 October, then the FOMC decision on 28 October (meeting 27-28 October); US Q3 GDP and September PCE on 29 October; RBA decision 3 November.
